texto: If every mosquito on earth disappeared right now, you'd still be itching tomorrow.
That itch isn't the mosquito. It's your own immune system, fighting her spit.
And nobody told it she's gone. Tonight, no wine by your ear.
That wine is usually a female. Only females bite. The males have never tasted blood.
And soon, your dog would never need heartworm pills again.
Sharks kill about six people a year. Mosquitoes kill about that many every five minutes.
Over 600,000 people a year. Mostly small kids. And nature?
Scientists looked for anything that truly needs mosquitoes and came up nearly empty.
Frogs and bats would just eat other bugs. One orchid would lose a helper.
Mosquitoes carry its pollen, glued to their eyes. And no, you wouldn't lose chocolate.
It's pollinated by midges. Nature's big winners live up north,
where caribou climbed windy ridges just to escape the swarms.
So who would actually miss mosquitoes? Mostly the germs riding inside them.
